narration.en: Every truth table you write can be built with tiny switches. A logic gate is the hardware form of a connective; wire a few together and you get a circuit that decides.

body.en: A logic gate is an electronic circuit with one or more binary inputs and one output. NOT gives the complement (A'). AND gives A·B (1 only when all inputs are 1). OR gives A + B (0 only when all inputs are 0). NAND and NOR are AND and OR followed by NOT. XOR gives 1 when the inputs differ (A ⊕ B = A'B + AB'); XNOR gives 1 when they are equal. In Boolean notation · is AND, + is OR and a dash or prime is NOT.

body.en: NAND and NOR are called universal gates because any Boolean function can be built using only NAND gates (or only NOR gates). With NAND: NOT A = (A·A)'; AND = NOT of NAND; OR = (A'·B')' by De Morgan. This matters in manufacturing: a chip made from one kind of gate is cheaper and simpler. Chapter 2 of Class XII returns to universal gates in detail.
